title: Luca Guadagnino Discusses Artificial, Sam Altman and AI Anxiety
excerpt:
The Artificial director discusses his film about OpenAI's founders and its change of studio.
He also addresses Sam Altman's objections and his own concerns about artificial intelligence.
body_md:
Luca Guadagnino has discussed Artificial on Deadline's Crew Call podcast, describing a drama built around the personalities and conflicts associated with OpenAI, including Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk. The filmmaker sees the story as one about ambitious young scientists dealing with extraordinary influence and their own human flaws.

After festival presentations in New York and London, the film is scheduled for a limited theatrical release on December 25, 2026, through NEON. Early critical response cited in the report has been positive, adding to interest in the project ahead of its opening.

Amazon MGM Studios previously stepped away from the film. Guadagnino says he accepted the change without resentment and appreciated that the project could seek a new home rather than be abandoned. According to the director, NEON showed early enthusiasm after screening the finished work.

Altman has separately denied pressuring Amazon to leave the project. He has also disputed a trailer scene suggesting that his property contains a bunker displaying firearms. Guadagnino says the production took care to review sensitive material legally, but the contrasting accounts underscore the distinction between a dramatized movie and a verified historical record.

Andrew Garfield plays Altman, who has joked about encountering a convincing lookalike during filming near his home. The director also discusses his unease about artificial intelligence, relating those concerns to memories of growing up amid Cold War fears.
